correctness.rationale: Cycle type bijects isomorphism classes with integer partitions under the stated uniform law. Deletion and inclusion–exclusion give exact tail and prescribed-multiplicity counts even when shifts exceed n, using p(k)=0 for k<0. For the ratio, the leading Rademacher term with x=n−1/24 and c=π√(2/3) is exp(c√x)/(4√3 x) times (1−1/(c√x)), up to exponentially subleading error; taking a fixed shift changes the main exponential by 1−ch/(2√n)+O_h(n^(-1)) and the prefactors by 1+O_h(n^(-1)). A prescribed multiplicity at length j therefore costs πj/√(6n)+O(n^(-1)), while the two-length mixed difference cancels both constant and linear-shift terms. Effective bounded-degree Hanf locality gives a radius ρ and saturation t. The Gaifman balls in cycles of length ≤2ρ+1 are the whole directed cycles and in larger cycles are identical directed paths, with the radius-zero loop case distinguished. Thus short-type counts are j a_j and the long-type count is the total number of vertices in longer cycles. If fewer than t such vertices occur, their parts come from a finite list and all other parts are bounded in size, giving only polynomially many partitions against exponential-in-√n p(n). At order n^(-1/2) only the finitely many isolated short-type deficiencies matter, each evaluated on its explicit representative. This yields the stated effective weighted integer sum and its sign, with all other events contributing O_φ(n^(-1)). Absence of any prescribed m-cycle realizes (0,m), negation realizes (1,−m), and constants cover m=0. Nonzero coefficient forces the claimed sharp rate.
residual_risks: Finite arithmetic checks are not logical or asymptotic verification; the foregoing proof gives the fixed-sentence theorem. The constants do not give an error uniform over all ranks or sentences, and the law is not for uniform labeled permutations.

evidence: Burris–Compton–Odlyzko–Richmond give a qualitative 0–1 law for front-loaded admissible classes. Falgas-Ravry et al. obtain O(n^(-1)) convergence and finite rational limit spectra for specified polynomial-growth permutation classes in the two-order language.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Neither theorem dominates in the needed parameters: general front-loading guarantees only a limit, while the quantitative pattern-class result uses a different sample space and does not assign the target successor-language first correction.

originality.rationale: The qualitative law for the exact unlabelled model is known. Judged only on the effective first correction, its quantization and attainable spectrum, and the O(n^(-1)) remainder: inspected close sources do not cover or imply that combined quantitative result. A fixed multiplicity cap has a different limiting local law even though it uses the same logical machinery. This is best-of-knowledge, without dating-based priority inferences.
residual_risks: Compton's original Example 7.6 and the Woods full text could not be reviewed; a quantitative theorem could be hidden in the unavailable passages or other partition/logical-counting literature. The Hardy–Ramanujan DOI route was also unavailable; the standard leading Rademacher expansion was used in the correctness check, not claimed as new.

Bounded-multiplicity spectrum as the distinct comparison
value.rationale: A qualitative zero–one law leaves open whether finite structures approach it slowly, rapidly, or in a sentence-dependent continuum of leading coefficients. The theorem instead determines the complete discrete first-correction spectrum, a computable test for whether the leading term vanishes, and the resulting improvement to O(n^(-1)). It identifies exactly which local defects control the rate in a canonical unlabelled model, rather than tabulating a few examples.
residual_risks: No full asymptotic series, uniform error over sentences, or extension to order-enriched/MSO languages asserted.
